annotations.title: As they vvere miniſtring.
annotations.text: [1] If vve ſhould, as our Aduerſaries do, boldly turne vvhat text vve liſt, and flee from one language to an other for the aduantage of our cauſe, vve might haue tranſlated for miniſtring, ſacrificing. for ſo [2] the Greeke doth ſignifie, and ſo Eraſmus tranſlated. yea vve might haue tranſlated, Saying Maſſe, for ſo they did: and the Greeke Fathers hereof had their name, Liturgie, vvhich Eraſmus tranſlateth Maſſe, ſaying, Miſſa Chryſoſtomi. But vve keepe our text, as the tranſlators of the Scriptures ſhould do moſt religiouſly.

annotations.title: Separate me.
annotations.text: <mn>[1]</mn> Though Paul vvere taught by God him ſelf <mn>[2]</mn> and ſpecially deſigned by Chriſt to be an Apoſtle, and here choſen by the Holy Ghoſt together vvith Barnabas, yet they vvere to be ordered, conſecrated, and admitted by men. Vvhich vvholy condemneth al theſe nevv rebellious diſordered ſpirites, that chalenge and vſurpe the office of preaching and other ſacred actions from heauen, vvithout the Churches admiſſion.

notes.text: Paul & Barnabas are consecrated by men.

annotations.title: Faſting.
annotations.text: [1] Hereof the Church of God vſeth and preſcribeth publike faſtes at the foure ſolemne times of giuing holy Orders (vvhich are our Imber daies) as a neceſſarie preparatiue to ſo great a vvorke. as S. Leo declareth by this place, naming it alſo an Apoſtolical tradition. See. S. [2] Leo Ser. 9 de ieiunio 7 menſis, & Calixtus ep. 1. to. 1 Conc. Conc. Magunt. c. 34. 35. to 3. [3] And this faſting vvas not faſting from ſinne, nor moral or Chriſtian temperance, as the Proteſtants ridiculouſly affirme, for ſuch faſting they vvere bound euer to keepe: but it vvas abſtinence for a time from al meates or from ſome certaine kindes of meates, vvhich vvas ioyned vvith praier and ſacrifice, and done ſpecially at ſuch ſeaſons as the Church preſcribed, of al together (as in Lent, the Imber daies, Friday, Saturday) and not vvhen euery man liſt, as Aërius and ſuch Heretikes did hold.. S. Auguſt. har. 53.

notes.text: * Leo ep. 81. c. 1. Epipha. in compend. Leo ser. 3. et 4. de ieiu. 7. mensis.

annotations.title: Impoſing hands.
annotations.text: [1] Becauſe all bleſſings and conſecrations vvere done in the Apoſtles' time by the external ceremonie of impoſition of hands, diuers Sacraments vvere named of the ſame, ſpecially Confirmation, as is noted before, and [2] holy Ordering or conſecrating Biſhops, Prieſts, and Deacons, and Subdeacons, as vve ſee here and elſewhere. In vvhich though there were many holy words and ceremonies and a very ſolemne action: yet vvhatſoeuer is done in thoſe Sacraments, is altogether called impoſition of hands [3]: as vvhatſoeuer vvas done in the whole diuine myſterie of the B. [4] Sacrament, is named fraction of bread. For the Apoſtles (as S. Denys Eccl. hier. c. 1. in fine vvriteth) purpoſely kept cloſe in their open ſpeeches and writings which might come to the hands or ears of Infidels, the ſacred words and actions of the Sacraments. And S. Ambroſe ſaith, in 1. Tim. c. 4. The impoſition of the hand is myſtical words, vvherevvith the elected is conformed and made apt to his function, receiuing authoritie (his conſcience bearing vvitnes) that he may be bold in our Lord's ſtead to offer ſacrifice to God. And S. Hierom [5], The impoſition of hand is the Ordering of Clerks, Which is done by praier of the voice, and impoſition of the hand. And this is in ſome inferior orders alſo, but Paul and Barnabas were ordered to a higher function then inferior Prieſts, euen to be Biſhops throughout all Nations.

annotations.title: Sent of the Holy Ghoſt.
annotations.text: <mn>◦</mn> Vvhoſoeuer be ſent by the Church, are ſent of the Holy Ghoſt, though in ſuch an extraordinarie ſort it be not done. Vvhereby vve ſee hovv far the Officers of our ſoules in the Church do paſſe the temporal Magiſtrates, vvho though they be of Gods ordinance, yet not of the Holy Ghoſts ſpecial calling.
